text:
Deepak: kicking off a quick thread — onboarding q4_mixed 7B for RAG. primary goal is to hide retrieval latency by speculative decoding that uses a cached best-prefix from retriever top-k. A/B plan across NQ + ELI5 for quality, p95/p99 latency for infra.
Ana: nice. are we doing two-pass speculative or single-pass with soft-checks?
Deepak: two-pass. first pass greedy spec up to 16 tokens, then patch with retrieval when available. rollback on divergence > 0.6 (KL sim).
Mike: how are we handling KV cache sharding across GPUs? last time shards got stale during rollback and we saw corrupted attention.
Deepak: implemented a shadow-kv per request id. speculative tokens populate shadow KV; on commit we merge; on rollback we drop shadow and reapply commit path. adds ~1-2ms overhead.
Sara: can you paste the runtime config you used?
Deepak: sure — config snippet used in the canary: 
```json
{"model":"ozma-7b-q4_mixed","speculative":{"mode":"two-pass","max_spec_tokens":16,"rollback_threshold":0.6},"kv_shard_policy":"shadow-merge","batching":{"max_batch_size":8,"latency_slo_ms":120}}
```
Ana: nice. curious about quant accuracy — any hallucination spike on ELI5?
Deepak: small increase in unsupported claims. baseline fp16 exact-match on NQ: 62.1%, q4_mixed: 61.3% (delta -0.8). ELI5 factuality signal dropped ~1.2%. but p95 latency improved from 420ms -> 260ms for RAG end-to-end on small instances.
Eva: ops-bot: test cluster snapshot 2026-03-18 saved to canary-ozma7b-q4 (tags: spec-rag, q4m).
ops-bot: snapshot created: canary-ozma7b-q4-20260318 (sha: a1b2c3).
Mike: tradeoff looks reasonable for interactive features. what's the rollback rate?
Deepak: rollback happened on 9.6% of requests in the first run. avg rollback tokens 4.2. we see rollbacks cluster on long doc contexts where retriever latency > 120ms.
Sara: did you try prefix caching of retriever results to reduce mismatch?
Deepak: yes — prefix cache (per-user short-term TTL 30s) reduced rollback to 3.1% for repeat queries. cost: additional memory 120MB per node.
Ana: how about evaluation methodology — did you do paired evals or separate cohorts?
Deepak: paired. same prompts, run fp16 vs q4_mixed with deterministic seed, but speculative introduces non-determinism because of timing. we recorded seed+timing and discarded runs where retrieval arrival time variance >50ms. aim to keep apples-to-apples.
Mike: good call. any sample-level failure modes? examples?
Deepak: one case where speculative prefixed with an incorrect entity (predictive bias) and rollback corrected, but user-visible flash showed both tokens (speculative then fixed) — frontend needs to avoid rendering speculative tokens before commit. filed FE ticket.
Sara: is there a simple knob for rollout? like enable speculative only for requests with retriever latency > X?
Deepak: yes — rollout plan: start with heuristic "enable_speculative = retriever_latency_est > 80ms" and gradually lower. also metric: spec_commit_ratio and user-visible-flash_count.
Ana: any changes to quantization tuning? per-channel scale tweaks?
Deepak: tuned per-head qparams slightly to reduce KL on factual tokens; decayed per-layer scale on final 2 layers. improved EM by +0.2 vs naive q4_mixed.
Eva: ops-bot: canary deployment scheduled for 2026-03-19T02:00Z, canary size 20 nodes.
ops-bot: deployment scheduled (canary-ozma7b-q4 -> 20 nodes)
Mike: ok let's keep the canary running 24h with daily snapshots; I'll watch p95 and spec_rollback metrics. mark for postmortem if user-visible-flash_count > 0.1%
Deepak: thanks — next steps: add FE gating for speculative commit, run full NQ/ELI5 sweep with paired seeds 50k examples, push canary. I'll post logs in the eval dashboard.
